gold.user: A developer wants to retrieve a list of all existing relations in the Directus database to understand how different collections are linked.
gold.ideal: The response should include an array of relation objects, each detailing the source and target collections, as well as the type of relation.

gold.user: A database administrator needs to create a new relation between the 'users' and 'posts' collections to establish a one-to-many relationship.
gold.ideal: The response should confirm the creation of the relation and return the newly created relation object with its ID and details.

gold.user: A data analyst wants to fetch details of a specific relation by its ID to analyze how it affects data integrity between collections.
gold.ideal: The response should return the relation object corresponding to the provided ID, including all relevant metadata.

gold.user: A software engineer needs to update an existing relation to change its type from 'one-to-many' to 'many-to-many' to better reflect the data model.
gold.ideal: The response should indicate success and return the updated relation object with the new type and any other modified attributes.

gold.user: A project manager decides to remove an obsolete relation between 'products' and 'categories' as it is no longer relevant to the current data structure.
gold.ideal: The response should confirm the deletion of the relation and return a success message.
